summary: Aurora Payments - streaming disconnect bursts and fallback amplification during overnight payroll window
description: Issue summary: During Aurora Payments' scheduled overnight payroll batch (approx 00:45-01:20 UTC) customers observed repeated streaming disconnects and a rapid sequence of fallback completions that caused duplicate responses and an unexpected billing surge. Impact: ~18% of requests for Aurora's tenant returned either truncated streams or duplicate full completions for a ~35 minute window; downstream reconciliation systems reported duplicate payment authorizations which required manual dedupe. Environment: prod (eu-west-1), dedicated routing policy for enterprise tenants, mixed model variants (redwood-llm-v2 primary, rwd-embed-compact-v1 for embeddings). Timeline (high level): 00:43 - Traffic spike begins coincident with payroll job; 00:47 - First streaming reset alerts and elevated 5xx rate; 00:53 - Router began routing to fallback variant repeatedly; 01:05 - Billing spike detected by cost alert; 01:18 - Rolling policy adjusted, fallback dampening applied; 01:23 - Streaming stabilized and duplicate completions subsided. Steps to reproduce (reliable under load): 1) Recreate payload mix and rate from attached sample (see reproduction_payloads.zip in ticket attachments). 2) Simulate 600 req/min using redwood-llm-v2 pin with sequential long-context prompts (approx 1k tokens). 3) Observe gateway logs for stream-init failures and router policy logs for repeated fallback triggers. Logs & dashboards: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/streaming/aurora-payments?from=2026-03-10T00:30:00Z&to=2026-03-10T01:30:00Z; Wavefront alert: wf.alerts/stream-reset-rate; Kibana request dump: s3://incidents/aurora/2026-03-10/requests.gz
comments: 2026-03-10 00:50 - Aisha Malik (Support): Customer reported large number of truncated streams and duplicate completions. Asked for immediate traffic sample and confirmations about dedicated capacity. Aurora confirmed payroll run starting 00:45 UTC.

2026-03-10 00:56 - Rafael Gomez (SRE): Observed sudden increase in stream-init latency on eu-west routers and elevated 502/504 rates from serving-runtime. Noted repeated fallback routing to quantized variant under heavy tail latency. Opening incident INC-2026-03-10-AUR-01.

2026-03-10 01:08 - Customer (Aurora Ops): Confirmed duplicates in downstream ledger; requested urgent mitigation and billing mitigation. Asked for a rollback to pre-canary routing policy if that helps.

2026-03-10 01:20 - Rafael Gomez (SRE): Applied temporary fallback-dampening policy and increased concurrency cap for Aurora tenant on dedicated pool. Stream success rate recovered to baseline by 01:23. Asked customer to monitor for reconciliation drift.

2026-03-11 09:12 - Support Manager (Elena Cho): Provided preliminary impact summary and initiated follow-up with Billing and Account Management for credits. Scheduled postmortem for 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC.
2026-03-12 16:30 - Postmortem added by Rafael Gomez: Root cause analysis attached; action items assigned (see postmortem_actions).
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: burst traffic triggered an autoscaling jitter combined with a canary routing decision that preferred a lower-latency quantized variant but with a smaller KV cache, causing prefix cache misses and increased tail latency.

Findings: router logs show adaptive fallback counter for Aurora tenant incremented rapidly as 5xx/stream-resets hit threshold. Serving runtime metrics show a spike in KV cache miss ratio for redwood-llm-v2 around 00:48-01:02, corresponding to canary kernel selector choosing a memory-saver kernel for some shards.

Reproduce deterministically with stress harness: when simulating payroll pattern the router's fallback amplification loop (policy with low dampening factor) caused repeated re-routing; each fallback request created new cold KV cache on the fallback variant which then produced higher latency and additional resets, creating a positive feedback loop.
No evidence of tenant VM/GPU exhaustion in dedicated pool; pool still had spare capacity but eviction of warm cache happened due to variant switching and lower cache sizes on the fallback model.

Related configuration: a recent routing policy change (PR #4521) introduced a more aggressive fallback threshold to prioritize availability during degraded nodes — this interacted poorly with caches and long-context workloads.
Cross-check: linked SUP-70012 shows similar symptoms in a different tenant but resolved via increasing fallback dampening — provides precedent.
resolution: Short-term mitigation (01:20 UTC): applied tenant-level fallback dampening for Aurora, increased concurrency cap to reduce per-request queuing, and pinned Aurora to the warm variant profile for the duration of payroll window.
Rollback: reverted the most aggressive policy changes from PR #4521 in routing service for the eu-west rollout on 2026-03-10 03:00 UTC.
Customer communication: Support updated Aurora Ops at 01:30 UTC with mitigation steps and a recommendation to re-run reconciliation checks. Account team committed to billing review.
Monitoring: added a scoped dashboard with per-tenant fallback counter, KV cache miss ratio and stream-reset rate and an alert runbook to automatically apply dampening when pattern detected.

Permanent fix planned: change router fallback algorithm to be cache-aware (avoid immediate fallback if fallback variant has smaller cache size), and add canary gating for long-context workload profiles. Implementation tracked in github PR #4567.
postmortem_actions: Action 1: Engineering (Routing) to implement cache-aware fallback gating — owner: Rafael Gomez, ETA: 2026-04-02
Action 2: Product to publish recommended tenant profiles for overnight/high-burst jobs and add a 'payroll-safe' preset — owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-03-29
Action 3: Support & AM to apply a one-time billing credit for duplicate completions and refund disputed charges — owner: Marco Silva (Account), ETA: 2026-03-18
Action 4: Observability to add per-tenant canary dashboards and an automated dampening runbook — owner: Elena Cho, ETA: 2026-03-24
Action 5: SRE to add a resilience test to the chaos harness for variant-switch cold-cache scenarios — owner: SRE Team, ETA: 2026-04-09
billing_action: Account team approved a customer credit equal to the disputed token-based charges for the 00:45-01:25 UTC window; finance ticket FIN-8821 opened to process refund. Customer was offered a 3-month trial of reserved throughput at no additional charge as remediation.
